review.summary: The commit adds a missing `weighted_normal` method for embedded lines (SMatrix{dim,1} Jacobian, RefLine), fixing a MethodError raised when `reinit!` is called on FacetValues for an embedded line element. Issue #1226 documents the crash with a public-API MWE and PR #1235 states it fixes that issue. The change is a single hunk in src/FEValues/facet_integrals.jl, with an upstream test added in test/test_facevalues.jl covering both 2D and 3D embedded lines plus the error path for an invalid facet number.
review.evidence: Issue #1226: `MethodError: no method matching weighted_normal(::SMatrix{2,1,Float64,2}, ::Type{RefLine}, ::Int64)` from a public FacetValues reinit! call, so pre-fix behavior is a hard crash on an already-supported code path (embedded interpolations are supported elsewhere, e.g. CellValues). PR #1235 body: 'Fixes #1226 for 2D lines'. Minimization reports 1 of 1 hunk kept, globally minimal, all hunks necessary. Runtime evidence: stable_differential over 3 repetitions, full suite passes on the fixed revision. Upstream test asserts normals match finite-difference tangent directions for facets 1 and 2 at orders 1 and 2 in dim 2 and 3, and asserts ArgumentError for facet 3.
review.missing_evidence: PR number/title/body and commit stats are empty in the record, so the exact upstream commit message is unverified beyond the issue linkage. No pre-fix failure log text is included, only the classification 'stable_differential'. It is not shown whether other embedded reference shapes (e.g. embedded RefTriangle facets) remain unimplemented, which would indicate this is one slice of a broader incomplete feature.
review.validation_risks: The dedicated trigger calls the internal, unexported `Ferrite.weighted_normal` with a hand-built SMatrix rather than exercising the public FacetValues path from the issue MWE; this couples the trigger to an internal signature and could pass/fail for reasons unrelated to user-visible behavior. Interpretation risk: the issue title says 'not fully implemented', so a reviewer could classify this as completing an unimplemented capability rather than repairing regressed behavior; I treat it as a defect because the failure is a crash on an existing public API. The upstream test relies on atol=1.0e-6 finite-difference comparisons, a mild flakiness/tolerance sensitivity, though the trigger script avoids that by using exact equality.
review.suggested_tests: Reproduce the issue MWE directly: build a Line/QuadraticLine grid embedded in 2D and 3D, construct FacetValues with Lagrange{RefLine,order}() and a vector geometry interpolation, call reinit! for facets 1 and 2, and assert no exception plus getnormal equals the outward unit tangent. Assert the normal is unit-length and opposite in sign between facet 1 and facet 2. Verify getdetJdV on the facet is positive and finite. Keep the ArgumentError check for facet numbers outside 1:2. Optionally confirm normals are consistent with a curved (nonlinear) geometry via a finite-difference tangent at the endpoints.
